speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by asking: Have you noticed any blood in your urine, and is the pain in your right flank sudden or gradual? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine_Culture

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance is Reddish, WBC 10-20 /HPF, RBC Too numerous to count, Nitrites Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Positive. Urine_Culture: Not yet performed.

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or any recent illnesses. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying; since you denied fever or dysuria, has the pain radiated to your groin, and have you noticed any abdominal masses or changes in bowel habits? REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen/Pelvis with contrast

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Abdomen/Pelvis with contrast: Normal findings. No renal masses, hydronephrosis, or stones identified.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal CT scan and your denial of fever or urinary symptoms, have you noticed any clots in the urine, and does the pain worsen with physical activity or exercise? REQUEST TEST: Urine_Microscopy_Sediment

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urine_Microscopy_Sediment: Microscopic examination reveals numerous red blood cells, consistent with the "Too numerous to count" finding on the dipstick. The background shows 10-20 white blood cells per high-power field. No significant epithelial cells or casts are noted.
